description: Config for scripts/check-doc-drift.mjs — codifies Class #9 (multi-occurrence sibling-fix sweep) and Class #11 (multi-occurrence fix completeness). Each entry is one drift CHECK. Adding a new check is a config edit, not a code edit: append a new object with { id, kind, title, ... } where the remaining fields are the requiredFields declared by the handler module for that kind. The framework registers seven handler modules — source-vs-target-coverage, forbidden-pattern-in-targets, self-consistency, untagged-fence, helper-adoption-sweep, schema-conformance, framework-self-test — and dispatches each entry to the matching handler. New drift CLASSES (entirely new kinds of comparison) need both a config entry AND a new handler module; new INSTANCES of an existing class are config-only.

checks.title: All error codes documented
checks.description: Every error.code value emitted from packages/**/lib/errors.js (including STATE_MACHINE_<KIND> expansions, the D2/D1 batch + singleton collision/schema-invalid families, the DISPATCH_* union on DispatchPreconditionError, and the VALIDATOR_FAULT_* template-literal family on verify/index.js's runValidator helper) must appear in the error-codes handbook page. Stage C Wave A2.1 FX2 closed the vacuous-extractor root cause: the prior `reasons.push(`VALIDATOR_FAULT_` regex matched ZERO lines because verify/index.js pushes a *variable* (`reasons.push(faultReason)`) where the template literal lives in the runValidator helper a few lines up; the prior DISPATCH_* coverage was zero because no extractor existed at all (DispatchPreconditionError sets `this.code = opts.code` from a JSDoc-typed union, so the general `this.code = 'X'` literal extractor missed it). Fixed extractors target the MINT site (template-literal definition + JSDoc type union) rather than the assignment site, asserted non-vacuous by scripts/check-doc-drift.test.mjs's `error-codes META` test which strips each enforced code from the handbook and asserts drift fires.

The error-codes gate's source list covers: dogfood-swarm/lib/errors.js (typed class `this.code = 'X'` literals for IsolationError/CollectUpsertError/CliInvalidGlobsError, the STATE_MACHINE_${kind} template literal, AND the DISPATCH_* JSDoc-type-union string literals on DispatchPreconditionError — the class itself uses `this.code = opts.code` so the union IS the contract), ingest/validate-record.js + ingest/persist.js (typed class .code literals), findings/derive/write-findings.js + findings/synthesis/write-artifacts.js (the `this.code = 'X'` literals on the SCHEMA_INVALID + ID_COLLISION classes — caught by the general literal extractor, no per-code expand needed), and verify/index.js (the `VALIDATOR_FAULT_${cls}` template-literal definition in the runValidator helper — extracts at the MINT site, NOT the `reasons.push(faultReason)` callsite, because the latter pushes a variable and was vacuous pre-FX2).

checks.title: atomic-write helper adopted by all writers under packages/
checks.description: Every callsite that writes a file via raw fs.writeFileSync should go through atomicWriteFileSync from packages/findings/lib/atomic-write.js to avoid torn writes. Helper history: F-721047-010 sibling-fix gap. The allowlist captures known cross-fix-dependencies — Phase 7 wave 2 backend will retire each of these. Test fixtures (*.test.js) are auto-excluded.
checks.wrapperHint: Cross-package: import via @dogfood-lab/findings/lib/atomic-write.js. Same package: relative import. Wrappers that pin a component tag are allowed; the wrapper file must still import the helper. Phase 7 wave 2 W2-BACK-003: 6 dogfood-swarm/ callers migrated to import the helper; allowlist shrunk from 13 to 6 entries (5 cross-domain pipeline/outputs callers + the helper itself remain). Verify/runner.js was confirmed STALE (no callsites in source) and removed entirely. Phase 7 wave 3 W3-PIPE-001/002 added: `findings/lib/file-lock.js` (the lock helper itself uses raw writeFileSync in atomicCreateLock — its purpose IS to be the choke point for cross-process exclusion, distinct from atomic-write's torn-write contract) and `ingest/lib/atomic-write.js` (sibling helper to findings/lib/atomic-write.js — cannot import the findings copy without creating a workspace dependency cycle since findings already depends on ingest). Feature pass FT-i: `report/cli.js` joins its sibling `report/build-submission.js` — `@dogfood-lab/report` is the consumer-side submission builder that intentionally carries NO dependency on the findings backend cycle; its `--output` write targets a user-specified local path (a CLI convenience, equivalent to a shell redirect), not the shared evidence store, so the torn-write contract that protects records/ + indexes/ does not apply.

checks.title: Agent JSON outputs (audit / feature / amend) conform to packages/schemas/src/json/agent-output.schema.json
checks.description: The canonical envelope is { domain, summary, [findings|features|fixes], ... }. Phase-7-wave-1 productization (F-252713-017): replaces silent normalization in collect.js with a structured AgentOutputValidationError pointing the agent at the canonical shape. The schema is permissive at top level (only `domain` + `summary` required) so it can govern audit, feature, AND amend outputs, with phase-specific $defs for the inner shapes. Stage C Wave A2 D4-004 closed the vacuous-gate root cause: previously this check carried `allowEmpty: true` and both target globs matched ZERO committed files — the gate was structurally green forever. Now `swarms/__schema-fixtures__/` ships 3 hand-curated positive fixtures (basic, audit-with-findings, amend-with-fixes) plus 1 negative fixture (invalid-missing-domain.json). The handler reads `negativeFilenamePattern` (default `^invalid-`): basenames matching that regex MUST fail Ajv validation. If a negative fixture passes, the gate emits `NEGATIVE_FIXTURE_PASSED` — proof that the schema loosened or the fixture went stale.
checks.hint: Match packages/schemas/src/json/agent-output.schema.json. Required at top level: domain, summary. Audit outputs add `findings[]` (with severity ∈ CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW and category ∈ AUDIT_CATEGORIES); feature outputs add `features[]`; amend outputs add `fixes[]` + `files_changed[]`. Live-run target glob expanded 2026-05-14 (study-swarm Prevention-A): wave-2 amend's coordinator-brief drift (fixes_applied vs fixes) was caught at collect-time after agents had already run — moving the schema-conformance check to CI fires the gate at push time so brief-vs-schema drift surfaces before agents are dispatched. Stage C Wave A2 follow-up: a positive fixture that no longer validates means the schema tightened without updating the fixture (fix one side); a negative fixture that validates means the schema loosened without updating the negative test (fix the schema or the fixture). F-5d126106: the live-run glob (swarms/swarm-*/wave-*/outputs/*.json) is listed in `allowEmptyGlobs` because it is STRUCTURALLY unmatchable in CI — swarms/.gitignore ignores `swarm-*/` wholesale, so no push can ever contain a file under that path. It still matches real files on a dev rig where swarm-*/ working dirs exist on disk, which is where `npm run verify` actually schema-checks live wave outputs; CI's job is limited to the committed swarms/__schema-fixtures__/*.json fixtures, which are NOT in allowEmptyGlobs and must always match at least one file.

checks.title: Honesty surfaces cross-ref package.json + cli.js (R9, v1.3.1)
checks.description: R9 productized the post-v1.3.0-release honesty sweep. The v1.3.0 bump stamped the gated surfaces (package.json ×8, sync-version, README version block) but left stale `v1.2.3` text on the *ungated* honesty surfaces (SHIP_GATE / SCORECARD / CLAUDE / site-config), shipping a release whose own SHIP_GATE 'version matches tag' row was false. Per the v1.3.0 lesson #5, hand-maintained current-state claims recur as drift at every bump until a gate cross-checks them against authoritative resolvers. This check is that gate. Each claim anchors to an *explicit* per-surface current-state pattern (NOT free-floating version strings) so historical references like 'release v1.2.3 cut 2026-05-20', 'since v1.2.0', and '`**v1.2.0**,'-style scope-historical mentions are left alone. The companion META test at scripts/check-doc-drift.test.mjs 'R9 LIVE META' mutates every configured claim's captured value to a stale stand-in and asserts the gate fires drift naming the surface — without that meta-loop, R9 would itself become a vacuous gate (v1.3.0 lesson #3, bit twice at the FIX layer).
